340:
(a) An establishment duly licensed by the city, or any other Georgia county or municipality, to sell malt beverages or wine, or both, by the drink for consumption only on the premises may obtain a special event permit from the city entitling the establishment to sell malt beverages or wine, or both, off the premises during the course of a special event.
(b) Definitions. The following definitions are applicable to this section:
Malt beverage means an alcoholic beverage as defined by OCGA § 3-1-2(13), as amended.
Permittee means the person to whom a special event permit is issued by the city, and, in the case of a partnership, corporation, or other legal entity, this definition includes all partners, officers, and directors of such entity.
Special event means an organized activity having as its purpose entertainment, recreation, or education which takes place on public or private property, including, but not limited to, concerts, fairs, festivals, holiday celebrations, parties, and receptions.
Wine means an alcoholic beverage as defined by OCGA § 3-1-2(24), as amended.
(c) Application process.
(1) To be eligible to obtain a special event permit, the applicant must first obtain a license issued by the governing authority of the city, or any other Georgia county or municipality, authorizing the establishment to sell malt beverages or wine, or both, by the drink for on-premises consumption.
(2) The application for a special event permit must be submitted to the city clerk for review at least thirty (30) days prior to date of the special event. Provided, however, that the city, in its sole discretion, may accept applications for special event permits submitted within thirty (30) days of the date of the special event if the event is conducted or sponsored by the city or any local authority.
(3) Each application must be accompanied by cash or a certified check in the amount of twenty-five dollars ($25.00) for the application fee. This fee defrays the costs incurred in by the city in reviewing the application, performing background investigations, and related matters by the building inspector, and, potentially, if a denied application is appealed, by the city manager. The application fee is nonrefundable. If a permit is granted, an additional permit fee of fifty dollars ($50.00) for each day during which the special event will take place must also be paid by cash or a certified check. The permit will not be granted until the permit fee is paid in full. Provided, however, that the city may, in its sole discretion, waive the additional permit fee if the event is conducted or sponsored by the city or any local authority.
(4) Each application must be accompanied by a site plan specifying the exact location where the applicant proposes to sell, and patrons will consume, malt beverages or wine, or both, during the course of the special event, a security plan, which must be approved by the director of public safety or his or her designee, and a traffic plan. If the permit is granted, the location where the malt beverages or wine will be sold and consumed must be clearly marked for patrons.
(5) The city clerk must review, and either approve or deny, the application in writing within five (5) business days. If the application is denied, then the clerk must state the reason for denial in writing.
(6) An applicant may appeal the clerk's denial of a permit to the city manager. The appeal must be submitted in writing to the city manager within three (3) business days following denial of the application. The city manager, whose decision on the appeal is final, must review, and either affirm or reverse, the city clerk's denial of the application within five (5) business days following receipt of the appeal.
(d) Conditions for sale of malt beverages and wine during a special event.
(1) It is unlawful to sell or dispense malt beverages or wine at a special event without first obtaining a special event permit from the city.
(2) It is unlawful for a permittee to sell or dispense malt beverages or wine in any manner other than as authorized by a special event permit.
(3) All sales of malt beverages and wine by a permittee at a special event must take place within the defined areas of the special event location as designated on the application for the special event permit and no patron of the special event is allowed to leave the special event location with any malt beverages or wine.
(4) All sales of malt beverages and wine by a permittee at a special event must take place within the hours and days during which the sale of malt beverages and wine by the drink for consumption on the premises is otherwise permitted under section 4-111 of this chapter.
(5) Food must be served during any period of time that malt beverages or wine are offered for sale by a permittee.
(6) At least one (1) person per one hundred (100) persons attending the special event must serve as a security person for the special event.
(7) The special event permit is valid only for the length of the special event as designated on the application, not to exceed three (3) consecutive days.
(8) No more than five (5) special event permits will be issued to any applicant within any calendar year.
(9) After expiration of the special event, a permittee must apply for a new special event permit in the same manner as the original permit to sell malt beverages or wine at a subsequent special event.
(10) Permittees must comply with all provisions of this section, all other applicable provisions of chapter 4 of the LaFayette City Code pertaining to the sale of alcoholic beverages, and all state laws governing the sale of malt beverages and wine.
(e) Enforcement.
(1) A special event permit may be immediately revoked by the director of public safety, or his or her designee, for due cause for a violation of this section, any other applicable provision of the LaFayette City Code, or state law which results in an emergency situation in which the continued exercise of the privileges granted under a special event permit endangers the health, welfare, or safety of the public.
(2) Any person in violation of any provision of this section is guilty of an ordinance violation, and subject to a fine of up to one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) or six (6) months in jail, or both, per violation.
(3) Any person in violation any provision of this section may also, after hearing as provided in this chapter, have their malt beverage or wine license, or occupational tax certificate, or both, suspended or revoked.

(c) The city license issued under this division must, at all times, be kept plainly exposed to view to the public at the place of business of the licensee.
(Ord. No. 18-10, § 3, 12-10-2018)
356:
(a) Each application for a license under this division must be accompanied by a certified check for the full amount of the appropriate license fee, together with a separate check or cash in the amount of one hundred fifty dollars ($150.00) to defray investigative and administrative costs. If the application is denied and the license refused, or if the applicant withdraws his application prior to the license being issued, the license fee shall be refunded, but the one hundred fifty dollars ($150.00) cost paid for investigative and administrative fees shall be retained by the city. However, any person applying for more than one (1) license at the same time shall pay only one (1) fee to defray investigative and administrative expenses. (c) Once a license has been issued, however, no portion of the license fee will be refunded if the license is revoked, suspended, or surrendered.
(Ord. No. 18-10, § 3, 12-10-2018)
357:
(a) Applications for the sale of distilled spirits for consumption on the premises license must be made in writing to the city clerk or a designee for the privilege of engaging in the sale of distilled spirits for consumption on the premises using forms approved and furnished by the city clerk.
(b) The application must be filed with the city clerk along with the applicable application fee.
(c) The application must state:
(1) As to the applicant: Full name, age, home address, business address, telephone number, place of permanent residence, date of establishment of permanent residence at said location, address of last place of residence, name of spouse and all minor children, complete record of all convictions, guilty pleas and pleas of nolo contendere for violation of all laws, city, state and federal, of applicant and of applicant's spouse. If the applicant is a partnership said information shall be furnished as to each partner. If the applicant is a corporation said information must be furnished as to each director, each officer, and each stockholder who owns or controls ten (10) percent or more of the issued and outstanding stock of said corporation.
(2) As to applicant's proposed establishment manager or managers (if not same as applicant): Full name, age, home address, business address, telephone number, place of permanent residence, date of establishment of permanent residence at said location, address of last place of residence, name of spouse and all minor children, complete record of all convictions, guilty pleas and pleas of nolo contendere for violation of all laws, city, state and federal, of outlet manager's spouse.
(3) Exact location (street address) of proposed business establishment.
(4) Name and address of owner or landlord and resident manager, if any, of property proposed for location and whether or not there is a building proposed to be used already erected thereon.
(5) Name or trade name under which the proposed business shall be operated.
(6) Name and address of all persons having any financial interest in the business by way of ownership of building or stock, receipt of income from business or otherwise. This shall not apply to any stockholder who owns less than ten (10) percent of the issued and outstanding stock of the corporation.
(7) If the applicant is a corporation, the address of the principal place of business, the registered office, and the name of the registered agent or agents of the corporation.
(8) Such other information as may be required from time to time by the city through interrogatories or otherwise.
(d) The application must be sworn to by all applicants.
(e) A copy of applicant's license, application for license, or proposed application for a license from the State of Georgia, if one is required, must be attached to the application.
(Ord. No. 18-10, § 3, 12-10-2018)
358:
(a) In addition to evaluating the criteria required to be included with an application under section 4-152 of this division in reaching its final determination as to whether or not to grant an initial license application, the city will also be guided by the following factors:
(1) The proximity of other establishments licensed hereunder.
(2) The nature of the neighborhood immediately adjacent to the proposed location, that is, whether the same is predominantly residential, industrial or business.
(3) Whether the proposed location has adequate off-street parking facilities or other parking available for its patrons.
(b) The following limitations apply to licensure under this division:
(1) Prohibited premises. It shall be unlawful to grant a license for the sale of distilled spirits for consumption on the premises where the proposed location does not have a front entrance to the premises which is clearly visible from a public street, road or highway.
(2) Prohibited persons. It shall be unlawful to grant a license for the sale of distilled spirits for consumption on the premises to:
(A) A person who is not a citizen of the United States for a period of twelve (12) months next preceding the date of filing of the application, and if the applicant is a partnership these requirements apply to all partners in said business, whether a general partner or a limited partner; however, the provisions of this subsection shall not apply to a corporation.
(B) A corporation which is not duly qualified to do business in the State of Georgia and which is not in good standing with all of the rules and regulations of the Georgia Corporation Code and the Secretary of State of Georgia, and which does not have a registered agent for service of process within Walker County, Georgia; however, the provisions of this subsection shall not apply to an individual or a partnership which has no corporate partners.
(C) A person who has been convicted of a felony, or any crime of moral turpitude, within ten (10) years immediately prior to the filing of said application.
(D) A person who has been convicted or who has entered a plea of guilty or nolo contendere for any felony or any misdemeanor involving the illegal possession, transportation or sale of any alcoholic beverages, or taxability thereof within ten (10) years immediately prior to the filing of said application.
(E) A person who has been convicted or who has entered a plea of guilty or nolo contendere for any felony or any misdemeanor involving the illegal possession, transportation or sale of any drug, narcotic or controlled substance within ten (10) years immediately prior to the filing of said application.
(F) A person, partnership or corporation whose license under this division has been revoked for cause or who has had a license of any type under this division revoked for cause within five (5) years immediately prior to the filing of the application.
(G) A person who is under the age of twenty-one (21) years.
(H) A person who has been declared incompetent by a court of competent jurisdiction.
(I) An elected official, police officer, or other law enforcement officer of the city.
(J) If the applicant is a corporation, subsections (C) through (I), above, do not apply.
(K) Any partnership or corporation where any person has an interest, either as owner, partner, stockholder, director, or officer, or his or her spouse, has, within ten (10) years immediately prior to submission of an application, been convicted or has entered a plea of guilty or nolo contendere for any:
(i) Felony;
(ii) Crime of moral turpitude;
(iii) Misdemeanor involving the manufacturing, possession, transportation or sale of distilled spirits or the taxability thereof;
(iv) Misdemeanor involving the illegal possession, transportation, or sale of any drug, narcotic, or controlled substance; or
(v) Violation of this division.
(Ord. No. 18-10, § 3, 12-10-2018)
359:
(a) All licenses are issued for a period of one (1) year, the same to be a calendar year, running from January 1 through December 31, and shall be renewable as a matter of course upon payment of the appropriate fee, except as is hereinafter set out in subsection (d) of this section and as otherwise provided in this division.
(b) Each licensee must make written application for renewal on or before October 1 of each year on forms approved by the city clerk.
(c) The renewal application will be referred to the director of public safety or a designee, who will report on the licensee's activity, if any, and upon activity at the location of the licensed business, if any, during the year.
(d) If the director of public safety or designee reports any activity which constitutes probable cause for not renewing a license, the renewal will not be made, and the matter will be referred to the city for its consideration. A public hearing on the denial of a non-renewal will be held no later than December 31.
(e) The city will afford the licensee a public hearing after which the city may grant or deny for cause the renewal of any license issued under this division.
(f) In passing upon the application for renewal, the city will consider all evidence presented at the public hearing and will be guided by the following factors:
(1) All matters contained in sections 4-154 and 4-155 of this division; and
(2) Such evidence as is obtained and presented to the city as the result of the investigation provided for in subsection (c) of this section.
(Ord. No. 18-10, § 3, 12-10-2018; Ord. No. 21/03, § 5, 10-11-2021)
360:
(a) License suspensions initiated by the director of public safety, code enforcement officer, or a designee.
(1) The director of public safety, code enforcement officer, or a designee may suspend and seize any retail license to sell distilled spirits for consumption on the premises if, at any time during the holding of a license granted under this division, it should appear that the licensee has:
(i) Violated the provisions of this division;
(ii) Violated any laws of the State of Georgia or any federal laws involving possession, transportation or sale of any alcohol, alcoholic spirits, prohibited liquors, alcoholic beverages or taxability thereof or involving illegal possession, transportation or sale of any drug, narcotic or controlled substance;
(iii) Become a person, firm or corporation prohibited by this division from having a license granted to him, her, or it;
(iv) Submitted an application containing known false information; or
(v) Engaged in conduct detriment to the health, safety, or welfare of the public.
(2) If the licensee is dissatisfied with such suspension, the licensee may appeal to the city council by filing a written request with the city clerk stating the grounds and reasons.
(3) The city council will hold a hearing on the suspension within ten (10) days of the filing of the appeal, after which the city council has the full authority and power to revoke, refuse to renew, further suspend, or place on probation any license which has been suspended as provided by this subsection.
(4) The city council must make its final determination within ten (10) business days of the completion of the appeal hearing.
(b) Adverse licensure actions initiated by the city council.
(1) In addition to the procedures provided in subsection (a), the city council may, of its own volition, suspend, revoke, or not renew a license issued under this division following a hearing.
(2) A notice explaining the proposed adverse action, i.e. suspension, revocation, or non-renewal, and the time and place designated for the hearing must be issued to the licensee in writing.
(3) The written notice must set forth, in reasonable detail, the ground or grounds for the proposed adverse action and the factual basis supporting the ground or grounds; and advise the licensee of the right to present evidence, witnesses, and arguments and to be represented by counsel at the hearing.
(4) The hearing will not be held prior to the passage often days following the date of notice of the proposed adverse action.
(5) The city council must make its final determination within ten (10) business days of the completion of the hearing.
(6) The city council's decision must be personally served, mailed by certified mail, return receipt requested, or by overnight delivery to the licensee and his attorney, with a copy to the city attorney, within ten (10) business days of the close of the hearing.
(7) The decision of the city council constitutes final action by the city, subject to review upon petition for certiorari to the Superior Court of Walker County, Georgia.
(c) Upon receipt of notice of adverse action against the licensee under this section, the licensee may waive its right to a hearing and stipulate to a sanction, as recommended by the city clerk in consultation with the director of public safety. Any stipulation entered under this subsection shall be in writing, signed by the licensee, and is not appealable.
(d) Except as provided in subsection (a) of this section, no license will be suspended, revoked, or non-renewed without the opportunity for a hearing as provided in this section.
(Ord. No. 18-10, § 3, 12-10-2018; Ord. No. 21/03, § 5, 10-11-2021)
361:
(a) Distilled spirits may only be sold in the following types of retail establishments:
(1) Eating establishments, including those located within a hotel or motel if every entrance to the eating establishment within the hotel or motel is from a public lobby, hallway, mall, or other publicly used interior portion of the primary use structure; or
(2) An indoor nonprofit civic and cultural center qualified under Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code capable of serving prepared food, with a full-service kitchen prepared to serve food every hour they are open and deriving at least seventy (70) percent of its total annual gross sales from the sale of prepared meals or foods and recreation activities.
(b) Distilled spirits may only be sold for consumption on the premises where sold in areas zoned as "business" or in a zoning district which permits eating establishments as conforming uses or where an eating establishment is incidental to a hotel or motel.
(c) Prohibited locations. It is unlawful to grant a license for the sale of distilled spirits by the drink within the following areas in the city:
(1) Within fifty (50) feet of any school building or school grounds, as measured by the most direct route of travel on the ground.
(2) Within one hundred (100) yards of any alcoholic treatment center owned and operated by the city, Walker County, Georgia, or the State of Georgia, as measured by the most direct route of travel on the ground.
(3) Within one hundred (100) yards of any housing authority property, as measured by the most direct route of travel on the ground.
(Ord. No. 18-10, § 3, 12-10-2018; Ord. No. 19-08, § 5, 10-10-2019)
362:
(a) Distilled spirits must not be sold or distributed for consumption on the premises except Monday through Saturday between the hours of 10:00 a.m. through 12:00 midnight.
(b) The sale or distribution of distilled spirits for consumption on the premises is not be permitted on:
(1) Sundays;
(2) Election days within the city during the hours the polls are open; and
(3) Christmas day.
(Ord. No. 18-10, § 3, 12-10-2018)
363:
(a) It is unlawful for any person to sell or possess for the purpose of sale any distilled spirits if the person does not have a license granted by the city to sell or possess for sale distilled spirits or to make deliveries beyond the boundaries of the premises covered by the license.
(b) No person shall allow or require a person in his employment under eighteen (18) years of age to dispense, serve, sell, or take orders for any distilled spirits.
(c) It is a violation of this division not to require and properly check identification for such persons as reasonably necessary to ensure that an underage person is not sold, served, or does not have in his possession distilled spirits while in a licensed establishment. But nothing in this section requires mandatory checking of the identification of every customer.
(d) It is prohibited for any person to bring his or her own distilled spirits in any establishment, i.e. brown-bagging, regardless of whether such establishment is licensed or unlicensed to serve distilled spirits by the drink.
(e) No licensee shall keep any distilled spirits at any place except the licensed place of business.
(f) No licensee shall buy, arrange to buy, or in any way affect the transfer of any distilled spirits except from a licensed wholesaler.
(g) Any violation of the provisions of this division may, upon determination of violation, result in suspension or revocation of a license issued under this division; or the council may in lieu of suspension or revocation thereof impose a civil penalty of not less than five hundred dollars ($500.00) nor more than one thousand dollars ($1,000.00).
(Ord. No. 18-10, § 3, 12-10-2018)
364:
(a) No person shall be employed to dispense distilled spirits or serve in any managerial position by an establishment holding a license under this division until such person has been fingerprinted and cleared by the director of public safety for the city or his designee or city code enforcement officer indicating that the person is eligible for such employment as per the minimum requirements for an applicant under this division.
(b) No permit shall be issued until such time as a signed application has been filed with the city clerk or designee and upon payment of a fee in the amount of fifty dollars ($50.00) and a search of the criminal record of the applicant completed. The application shall include, but shall be limited to, the name, date of birth and prior arrest record of the person, though the fact of an arrest record shall be used for investigative purposes only, and shall give rise to no presumption or inference of guilt. Due to the inclusion of the arrest information, the application shall be regarded as confidential and shall not be produced for public inspection without a court order.
(c) The city clerk or a designee shall have a complete and exhaustive search made relative to any criminal record of the person fingerprinted. If the person is eligible for employment, the city clerk or a designee shall issue a permit to the person, by mail, stating that the person is eligible for employment. If it is found that the person is not eligible for employment, the director of public safety or city code enforcement officer or other designee shall notify the person, in writing, that he or she is not eligible for employment, the cause of such denial and his or her right of appeal.
(d) No person shall be granted a pouring permit unless it appears to the satisfaction of the city clerk or a designee that such person has not been convicted or pled guilty or entered a plea of nolo contendere to any crime involving moral turpitude, illegal gambling, illegal possession or sale of controlled substances or the illegal sale or possession of alcoholic beverages, including the sale or transfer of alcoholic beverages to a minor in a manner contrary to law, keeping a place of prostitution, solicitation of sodomy, or any sexually related crime within a period of five (5) years preceding the date of the application and is not on probation or parole. A person's first-time conviction for illegal possession of alcohol as a misdemeanor or violation of a city or county ordinance shall not, by itself, make a person ineligible for an alcohol pouring permit. No person shall be granted a pouring permit who has been convicted, plead guilty or entered a plea of nolo contendere to any federal, state, or local law for any felony within five (5) years preceding the date of the application and is currently on probation or parole. For purposes of this division, a conviction or pleas of guilt or nolo contendere shall be ignored as to any offense for which a person whose sentence was entered under the Georgia First Offender Act, as amended. Except, however, that any such offense shall not be ignored if the person violated any term of probation imposed by the court granting first offender treatment or committed another crime and the sentencing court entered an adjudication of guilt as to the crime for which the person had previously been sentenced as a first offender.
(e) An alcohol pouring permit shall be issued for a period of three (3) calendar years from the date of the application. As provided in subsection (j) of this section, the alcohol pouring permit must be in the possession of the employee while the employee is working at the licensed establishment and available for inspection by members of the city police department. After application of the pouring permit is completed with the city, the employee may immediately commence work on a temporary basis provided the employee retains the receipt for the permit on his or her person at all times at the premises for which the alcohol license has been issued, and thereafter, if a permit is issued, must maintain on his or her person at the premises the actual pouring permit. If a permit is not issued, the employee must immediately cease work upon being notified that a permit will not be issued to the employee.
(f) No person shall be issued a permit if it is determined that the person falsified, concealed or covered up any material fact by any device, trick or scheme while making application to the city clerk for an alcohol beverage pouring permit under this section. If it is determined that a person is in violation of this subsection and a permit is denied for this reason, then ninety (90) calendar days must elapse from the date of notification of the denial of the permit before the person may submit a new application for a permit.
(g) All permits issued through administrative error can be immediately terminated and seized by the city clerk or designee.
(h) Replacement permits will be issued within thirty (30) days of original date, upon paying one-half (½) of the fee charged for alcohol pouring permits. After thirty (30) days of original application date, a new application and fee must be submitted.
(i) All permits issued under this division remain the property of the city and shall be produced for inspection upon the demand of any city police officer, city code enforcement officer, city clerk or a designee.
(j) No licensee shall allow any employee or manager required to hold a permit to work on premises unless the employee or manager has in his or her possession a current valid city pouring permit. For new employees, a receipt issued by the city clerk may be used for a maximum of ninety (90) days from the date of its issue unless notified that a permit will not be issued. Licensees are required by this division to inspect and verify that each employee required to do so has in his or her possession a valid current alcohol pouring permit.
(k) It shall be the duty of all persons holding any license issued under this division to file with the city clerk the name of the establishment, the license number and a list of all employees, with their home addresses and home telephone numbers, twice annually during the month of June and again during the month of December.
(l) The permit issued under this section shall be issued to individuals only and as long as the permit is valid, may be used at any employer licensed by this division until said license is revoked, suspended, terminated, or expires.
(Ord. No. 18-10, § 3, 12-10-2018; Ord. No. 21/03, § 5, 10-11-2021)
365:
(a) Alcoholic beverage sales can be made by a licensed consumption on premises establishment in a patio/open area type environment if the establishment has been approved to do so by the code enforcement officer and is in compliance with any and all other regulations of the city. Also, all sales of distilled spirits under this provision must be in opaque containers and not in bottles or cans.
(b) The requirement for approval is that the patio/open area be enclosed by some structure providing for public ingress/egress only through the main licensed premises. The purpose of this requirement is to prevent a customer from leaving the outside sales area with an open drink without the licensee's knowledge.
(c) The height of such structure shall be a minimum of three and one-half (3½) feet above the patio floor, but the structure does have to shield or restrict visibility into or out of the patio/open sales area. The structure must be permitted and approved by the code enforcement officer and meet all building and fire code regulations.
(d) The only exit from the patio/open sales area is to be through the licensed establishment's main premises and through an approved fire exit, not for general public use unless an emergency exists. The fire exit must be of a type that sounds an alarm so that the establishment will be alerted in the event of unauthorized use when no emergency exists.
(Ord. No. 18-10, § 3, 12-10-2018)
366:
(a) It is prohibited for customers to leave the premises with open containers of distilled spirits, and it is the licensee's responsibility to ensure that no open containers of distilled spirits are sold and carried out of the premises.
(b) It is prohibited for customers to gather outside an establishment and consume distilled spirits.
(c) It is prohibited for the manager or any employee of a licensee to allow persons to gather outside an establishment and consume distilled spirits.
(d) This section does not apply to open area/outside sales as set forth in section 4-162 of this division.
(Ord. No. 18-10, § 3, 12-10-2018)
367:
The director of public safety, code enforcement officer, or their designees have the authority to enforce this division and to inspect establishments under this division. These inspections are to be made for the purpose of verifying compliance with the requirements of this division and state law. This section is not intended to limit the authority of any other officer to enforce this division or conduct inspections authorized by other provisions of this division or state law.
(Ord. No. 18-10, § 3, 12-10-2018; Ord. No. 21/03, § 5, 10-11-2021)
368:
The director of public safety or a designee may immediately close an establishment licensed under this division in case of emergency for the safety of the public, as determined in his or her sole discretion or to investigate a crime for a period of time not to exceed twenty-four (24) hours.
(Ord. No. 18-10, § 3, 12-10-2018; Ord. No. 21/03, § 5, 10-11-2021)
369:
(a) In addition to the license fees required in this division and in addition to the excise taxes levied by the state, there is hereby imposed an excise tax on the sale of distilled spirits.
(b) Excise taxes on the wholesale of distilled spirits. There is hereby levied an excise tax computed at the rate of twenty-two cents ($0.22) per liter which shall be paid to the city on all distilled spirits sold in the city. Such tax shall be paid to the city by the wholesaler on all distilled spirits sold to retail dealers in the city as follows:
(1) Each wholesaler selling, shipping, or in any way delivering distilled spirits to any retail dealer, shall collect the excise tax at the time of delivery to each retail dealer on or before the tenth day of the month following.
(2) The twenty-two cents ($0.22) per liter rate shall be prorated so that all containers of distilled spirits shall be taxed on the basis of twenty-two cents ($0.22) per liter.
(3) It is unlawful for any wholesaler to sell, ship or deliver in any manner any distilled spirits to a retail dealer without collecting the tax. It shall be unlawful for any retail dealer to possess, own, hold, store, display, or sell any distilled spirits on which such tax has not been paid.
(4) The wholesale dealer shall keep true and correct records of all sales and shipments of distilled spirits to licensees hereunder and shall render a sworn statement of the truth and accuracy of the report accompanying the monthly report to the city, and said report shall show the exact quantities of distilled spirits, by size and type of container and the amount of excise tax collected.
(5) The city shall have the right to audit and to require production of records from each wholesaler supplying licensees hereunder within the city and also from each licensee hereunder so supplied with distilled spirits by each wholesaler.
(6) Failure to make a timely report and remittance of the above taxes renders a wholesale dealer liable for a penalty equal to ten (10) percent of the total amount due, in addition to the amount of tax due; and, additionally, if a report is not filed or if taxes are not remitted and paid within thirty (30) days from the date either is due, the city has the right to suspend or revoke any wholesale license and further to prohibit the wholesaler from making any deliveries of any type whatsoever within the corporate limits of the city.
(c) Excise taxes on retail sales of poured distilled spirits by the drink. There is hereby levied an excise tax computed at the rate of three (3) percent of the charge to the public on sales of distilled spirits by the drink made by pouring outlets.
(1) This tax does not apply to the sale of fermented beverages made in whole or in part from malt or any similar fermented beverage.
(2) Such tax shall be paid to the city by the pouring licensee on all distilled spirits sold to customers by the drink in the city on or before the tenth day of the month following such sales.
(3) It is unlawful for any pouring licensee to fail to pay such excise tax and no person shall sell at retail for consumption on the premises within the city any alcoholic beverage on which the taxes imposed by this division have not been paid.
(4) Every licensee under this division for the sale of distilled spirits in the city shall keep all invoices relating to each purchase of distilled spirits and such other records, receipts, invoices and other pertinent papers in such form as the city clerk may require.
(5) The city has the right to audit and to require production of records from each licensee.
(Ord. No. 18-10, § 3, 12-10-2018)
371:
(a) An establishment duly licensed by the city, or any other Georgia county or municipality, to sell distilled spirits by the drink for consumption only on the premises may obtain a special event permit from the city entitling the establishment to sell distilled spirits off the premises during the course of a special event.
(b) The procedure for obtaining a special event permit for the sale of distilled spirits is the same as that applicable to the sale of malt beverages and wine under article II, division 4, section 4-134, and the sale of distilled spirits during a special event is subject to the same conditions, terms, and restrictions applicable to the sale of malt beverages and wine under said section.
(Ord. No. 19-08, § 6, 10-10-2019)
374:
Distiller means a manufacturer of distilled spirts.

(Ord. No. 22/08, § 1, 6-13-2022)
375:
(a) The issuance of a distiller's license is authorized in the city.
(b) The ownership or operation of a distillery is prohibited in the city unless a distiller's license is obtained in accordance with the provisions of this division.
(c) Each holder of a distiller's license must comply with the provisions of this division and all applicable state statutes, including rules and regulations promulgated by the Georgia Department of Revenue.

376:
(a) To obtain a distiller's license, an application must be submitted to the city clerk for review.
(b) Each application must be accompanied by cash or a certified check in the amount of one hundred dollars ($100.00) for the application fee. This fee defrays the costs incurred in by the city in reviewing the application. The application fee is nonrefundable.

(Ord. No. 22/08, § 1, 6-13-2022)
377:
(a) Distilleries may not sell any alcoholic beverages except for distilled spirits that are produced at the distillery.
(b) Any distillery engaging in the retail sales distilled spirits under this section must remit all state and local excise taxes to the proper tax collecting authority.
(c) The sale of distilled spirits by a licensed distiller to a licensed retailer or retail consumption dealer for the purpose of resale is prohibited.
(Ord. No. 22/08, § 1, 6-13-2022)
378:
(a) As a limited exception to the provisions of this chapter which implement and enforce the three-tier system for the manufacture, distribution, and sale of distilled spirits established under state law, a distiller's license authorizes the holder of such license to sell directly to the public on its licensed premises up to five hundred (500) barrels of distilled spirits manufactured on such licensed premises per year for consumption on the premises (sales by the drink) only.
(b) Such retail sales are permitted on the days and at the times that the retail sale of distilled spirits for consumption on the premises are authorized for other retailer licensees under this chapter.
(Ord. No. 22/08, § 1, 6-13-2022)
381:
It shall be unlawful for any person to allow or permit any horses, cattle, sheep, goats, or other livestock to run at large on the streets of the city, or to be staked so that they can go upon the streets of the city, or to drive or lead any such animals or livestock along or on the sidewalks in the city, or to drive or lead any such animals or livestock along and over the streets of the city, unless fastened to a rope, chain, or other substantial leading device. Any such rope, chain, or other substantial leading device must be securely held by a responsible person. Animals in violation of this chapter shall be impounded by members of the police department, other authorized employees or agents of the city, or the county animal control officers or their employees or agents.
(Code 1975, § 2-10)
382:
(a) If any animal impounded as provided in section 5-1 is not claimed and redeemed by the owner, or keeper thereof, within five (5) days after such impoundment, or when ownership of the animal is relinquished by the owner, the animal may be disposed of.
(b) As methods of disposal, the animal may be:
(1) Placed in an adoptive home or rescue organization;
(2) Sold; or
(3) Destroyed in a humane manner if, in the opinion of a licensed accredited veterinarian, the animal has a temperament or condition such that euthanasia is the only reasonable course of action.

A person inside a structure will not be considered under this section to have voice command over an animal that is outside. Close proximity means within a distance where the animal can respond to spoken (not shouted) commands.
(b) The following are the minimum standards for indoor shelter for animals:
(1) The ambient temperature must be compatible with the health of the animal.
(2) Indoor housing facilities must be adequately ventilated by natural or mechanical means to provide for the health of the animal at all times.
(c) All pets must have shelter available when tied or confined while unattended outdoors for any length of time.

(a) In addition to the requirements set forth in article II of chapter 5, the following safeguard actions must be taken by the owner of a vicious animal in recognition of the concern for the safety of the residents of the city:
(1) An owner or keeper of a vicious animal must keep the animal inside his or her residence at all times unless the animal is directly placed and kept within a secure enclosure. A secure enclosure means a securely enclosed pen, fence, or other structure of adequate size to humanely confine the vicious animal. The enclosure must prevent the entry of young children and be designed to keep the vicious animal from escaping. Any such pen or structure must have secure sides and a secure top attached to all sides. The sides must either be buried two (2) feet into the ground or sunken into a concrete pad. The gate to the enclosure must be inward opening and kept securely locked. If the animal is enclosed within a fence, all sides of the fence must be of sufficient height and the bottom of the fence must be constructed or secured in such a manner as to prevent the animal's escape from over or from under the fence, and all entry gates to the fence must be kept securely locked. Any such enclosure must also provide protection from the elements for the animal. An electric fence or similar technology, direct voice command, or tethering are not secure methods of enclosure for the vicious animal.
(2) The enclosure shall be completely surrounded by a separate perimeter fence. The enclosure may not share common fencing with the perimeter fence. The perimeter fence shall be of sufficient height to prevent the vicious animal from escaping by jumping over the fence. The perimeter fence shall be sufficiently secured to prevent the vicious animal from escaping by crawling or digging under or knocking over the fence. If there is a gate in the fence, the gate shall be kept securely locked.
(3) Except when being transported to a licensed veterinary facility, a vicious animal must not be allowed off the property of the owner or keeper. If transport for veterinary care be needed, the animal must be securely and humanely confined within a vehicle. Movement of the animal from the residence of the owner to and from the transporting vehicle and to and from the veterinary facility must be conducted with the animal securely leashed by a leash no longer than six (6) feet in length and muzzled by a muzzle or device constructed so as to prevent the animal from biting, or the animal is closed and locked in a cage or crate.
(4) Except as may be allowed in this article, the owner or keeper of a vicious animal must at all times keep the vicious animal within either the residence of the owner or keeper or the secure enclosure as set forth in this section. It is unlawful to permit the animal to be outside the residence or the secure enclosure of the owner or keeper unless the animal is properly muzzled by a muzzle or device constructed so as to prevent the animal from biting, and the animal is attended by the owner or keeper, who is capable of controlling the animal, and the animal is restrained by a secure collar and leash of sufficient strength to prevent escape. The leash must be no longer than six (6) feet in length. The animal must be kept at least fifteen (15) feet within the perimeter boundaries of the property unless the perimeter boundary is securely fenced.
(5) The owner or keeper of a vicious animal must maintain at all times either a policy of insurance or a surety bond in a minimum amount of fifty thousand dollars ($50,000.00) to cover claims for any personal injuries inflicted by the vicious animal, which policy or surety bond must be issued by an insurer or surety, as the case may be, authorized to transact business in this state. A copy of the insurance policy or surety bond, and all renewals thereof, must be provided by the owner or keeper to the city's animal control department.
(6) The premises where a vicious animal is kept must be posted with clearly visible signs warning that there is an animal on the premises that presents a danger to human beings. The signs must include a symbol sufficient to convey without words the message that there is an animal on the premises that presents a danger to human beings. The signs must be conspicuously displayed on each exterior side of the enclosure for each fifty (50) feet of the enclosure, with a minimum of two (2) signs, in addition to a sign on each ingress and egress point to the enclosure. The signs must be a minimum of ten (10) inches tall and fourteen (14) inches long. In addition, signs must be placed at each door to the house if the vicious animal is kept at any time in the house. The signs must also comply with the requirements set forth by the Georgia Department of Natural Resources. A copy of the Department of Natural Resources' sign requirements are available from the animal control department.
(7) The owner or keeper of a vicious animal must, prior to placing the animal on the premises, have the animal micro-chip registered, at the owner's expense, and provide the registration number to the city's animal control department. The owner or keeper must keep the micro-chip registration information updated and provide the city's animal control department with the updated registration information.
(b) In addition to the requirements set forth in article II of chapter 5, the following safeguard actions must be taken by the owner of a potentially dangerous animal in recognition of the concern for the safety of the residents of the city;
(1) An owner or keeper of a potentially dangerous animal must keep the animal inside his or her residence at all times unless the animal is directly placed and kept within a proper enclosure. A proper enclosure means a securely enclosed pen, fence, or other structure of adequate size to humanely confine the potentially dangerous animal. The enclosure must prevent the entry of young children and be designed to keep the potentially dangerous animal from escaping. Any such pen or structure must have secure sides and a secure top attached to all sides. The gate to the enclosure must be inward opening and kept secured. If the animal is enclosed within a fence, all sides of the fence must be of sufficient height and the bottom of the fence must be constructed or secured in such a manner as to prevent the animal's escape from over or from under the fence, and all entry gates to the fence must be kept secured. Any such enclosure must also provide protection from the elements for the animal. An electric fence or similar technology, direct voice command or tethering is not a proper method of enclosure for the potentially dangerous animal.
(2) Except as otherwise may be allowed in this article, the owner or keeper of a potentially dangerous animal must at all times keep the potentially dangerous animal within either the residence of the owner or keeper or the proper enclosure as set forth in this section. (a) Definitions. [As used in this section, the following words shall have the meaning ascribed thereto:]
(1) Commercial means any type of building other than residential.
(2) Construction means the erection of a new building or the alteration of an existing building in connection with its repair or renovation or in connection with making an addition to an existing building and shall include the replacement of a malfunctioning, unserviceable, or obsolete faucet, showerhead, toilet, or urinal in an existing building.
(3) Residential means any building or unit of a building intended for occupancy as a dwelling but shall not include a hotel or motel.
(b) Residential, prohibited installations. On or after July 1, 1991, no construction may be initiated within the city for any residential building of any type which:
(1) Employs a gravity tank-type, flushometer-valve or flushometer-tank toilet that uses more than an average of one and six tenths (1.6) gallons of water per flush; provided, however, this paragraph shall not be applicable to one-piece toilets until July 1, 1992;
(2) Employs a shower head that allows a flow of more than an average of two and one half (2.5) gallons of water per minute at sixty (60) pounds per square inch of pressure;
(3) Employs a urinal that uses more than an average of one and zero tenths (1.0) gallons of water per flush;
(4) Employs a lavatory faucet or lavatory replacement aerator that allows a flow or more than two and zero tenths (2.0) gallons of water per minute; or
(5) Employs a kitchen faucet or kitchen replacement aerator that allows a flow of more than two and one half (2.5) gallons of water per minute.
(c) Commercial, prohibited installations. On or after July 1, 1992, there shall be no construction of any commercial building initiated within the city for any commercial building of any type which does not meet the requirements of subparagraph (b)(1) through (5) of this section.
(d) Repair, renovation or addition. The requirement of subsection (b) shall apply to any residential construction initiated after July 1, 1991, and to any commercial construction initiated after July 1, 1992, which involves the repair or renovation of or addition to any existing building when such repair or renovation of or addition to such existing building includes replacement of toilets or showers or both.
(e) Exemptions. New construction and the repair or renovation of an existing building shall be exempt from the requirements of subsections (b), (c) and (d) when:
(1) The repair or renovation of the existing building does not include the replacement of the plumbing or sewage system servicing toilets, faucets or shower heads within such existing buildings; or
(2) When such plumbing or sewage system within such existing building, because of its capacity, design or installation would not function properly if the toilets, faucets or shower heads required by this section were installed; or
(3) Such system is a well or gravity flow from a spring and is owned privately by an individual for use in such individual's personal residence; or
(4) Units to be installed are:
a. Specifically designed for use by the handicapped;
b. Specifically designed to withstand unusual abuse or installation in a penal institution; or
c. Toilets for juveniles.
(f) Exemption application; inspection fee. The owner, or his agent, of a building undergoing new construction or repair or renovation who is entitled to an exemption as specified in subparagraph (e)(2), (3) or (4) of this section shall obtain the exemption by applying at city hall, City of Lafayette. A fee of twenty-five dollars ($25.00) shall be charged for the inspection and issuance of such exemption. The building official shall review the application, and deny said application or issue the exemption.
(g) Enforcement; penalty.
(1) This section shall be enforced by the building official for the city. Citations for violations may be issued by said building official.
(2) Any person, corporation, partnership or other entity violating this section shall be tried before the recorder's court of the city. Upon conviction, a violation of the section may be punished by a fine not to exceed one hundred dollars ($100.00) and or imprisonment not to exceed five (5) days.
